> **Pipeline step 02 — EDSM catch models (main text).**
>
> **Purpose.** Fit the 22 EDSM negative-binomial catch models (`fit_edsm_0` … `fit_edsm_21`),
> each with a `(1 | StationCode)` random intercept, and score them with grouped 5-fold
> cross-validation on a single, cached station partition so every model is compared on
> identical folds.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv`; the cached fold vector
> `fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_folds.rds` (rebuilt from a completed fit if absent).
>
> **Outputs.** `fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_<N>.rds`, `fits_edsm_Vfix/edsm_fits_Vfix_output.txt`,
> the small criteria bundle `fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_criteria_bundle.rds`, and
> `fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_topmods_catch_kfold5_station_comparisons.csv`.
>
> **Cost.** ~1–2 h per model including K-fold (6 extra fits each); all fitting chunks are
> `eval=FALSE`.
>
> **Appendix.** Salinity / temperature fits 22–26 and the water-year diagnostic fit 27 re-use
> the runner defined here; see `appendix_salinity_temperature_wateryear/A04_*.R`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(DHARMa)
library(lubridate)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Load the EDSM model dataset (4,241 tows; built by `00_data/01_build_model_datasets.Rmd`).
```{r load-data}
tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona <- read_csv("data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv")
```


EDSM CATCH U75 with 1|StationCode random intercept
Realized should probably have station as grouping factor because of multi-tow for EDSM.
We refit every model `fit_edsm_0` .. `fit_edsm_21` adding `+ (1|StationCode)` and evaluate
them with grouped (by StationCode) K-fold CV (K = 5) instead of PSIS-LOO, because there are
too many high-leverage points for moment matching (computation takes too long).
```{r priors}
catch_priors <- c(prior(normal(0,2.5), class = "b"),
                  prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = "shape"),
                  prior(normal(-5.5, 2), class = "Intercept"),
                  prior(normal(20, 5), class = "sds"))
```


###################################
Station-level K-fold helper.
The fold assignment is supplied as a precomputed vector (`folds`) so that EVERY model is scored
on the exact same partition of stations. This is what makes the K-fold model comparison valid.
########################################
```{r kfold-helper}
# Station-level K-fold cross-validation for brms models.
# `folds` must be an integer vector of length nrow(fit$data) giving the fold id (1..K)
# of each observation. Passing folds directly (rather than folds = "grouped") guarantees an
# identical partition across all fits, regardless of RNG state.
add_station_kfold <- function(
  fit,
  folds,
  K = 5,
  group = "StationCode",
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 3000,
  warmup = 2000,
  control = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
  seed = 123,
  save_fits = FALSE
) {
  stopifnot(length(folds) == nrow(fit$data))
  set.seed(seed)

  kf <- brms::kfold(
    fit,
    folds = folds,        # custom fold vector -> identical partition for every model
    compare = FALSE,
    save_fits = save_fits,
    chains = chains,
    cores = cores,
    iter = iter,
    warmup = warmup,
    control = control
  )

  # Stored under "kfold5_StationCode" to match the existing comparison code.
  fit$criteria[[paste0("kfold", K, "_", group)]] <- kf

  return(fit)
}
```


###################################
Canonical fold set.
Build the K = 5 grouped-by-StationCode fold vector ONCE and cache it to disk so every model
(including the appendix fits) is scored on the *exact* same folds. The folds are taken straight from a completed fit's stored
kfold object, so they are guaranteed identical; we also confirm seed 123 reproduces them.
########################################
```{r station-folds}
fold_rds <- "fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_folds.rds"

if (file.exists(fold_rds)) {
  station_folds <- readRDS(fold_rds)
} else {
  # One-time build (loads one ~190 MB fit). The "folds" attribute on a completed kfold object
  # IS the partition that was actually used, so this is the authoritative fold set.
  f_done <- readRDS("fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_8.rds")
  station_folds <- as.integer(attr(f_done$criteria[["kfold5_StationCode"]], "folds"))
  rm(f_done); gc()

  # Confirm that the seed used in the wrapper reproduces this exact assignment.
  set.seed(123)
  folds_seed <- as.integer(
    loo::kfold_split_grouped(K = 5, x = factor(tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona$StationCode))
  )
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(station_folds, folds_seed))) {
    message("Seed 123 reproduces the stored fold assignment exactly.")
  } else {
    message("NOTE: seed 123 did NOT reproduce stored folds; ",
            "saving the stored (authoritative) folds used by the completed fits.")
  }

  stopifnot(length(station_folds) == nrow(tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona))
  saveRDS(station_folds, fold_rds)
}

# Sanity check
table(station_folds)
```


###################################
Model definition table + runner.
`fit_defs` lists the fixed-effects portion of every model (fit 0..21), transcribed from the
original no-intercept formulas so this notebook no longer depends on those fits. The base model
appended to each is:
  n_l_75 ~ <fixef> + s(water_year_day) + offset(log(Volume)) + (1|StationCode)
########################################
```{r fit-defs-runner}
# Fixed-effects part of each model. "" = null model (smooth + offset + intercept only).
fit_defs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~num, ~fixef,
  0L,   "",
  1L,   "out30_z",
  2L,   "out30_z + distance_along_channel_z",
  3L,   "out30_z + distance_m_z",
  4L,   "out30_z + distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z",
  5L,   "out30_z * distance_along_channel_z",
  6L,   "out30_z * distance_m_z",
  7L,   "out30_z * distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z",
  8L,   "out30_z * distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z",
  9L,   "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z)",
  10L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + secchi_z",
  11L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + habitat2020 + secchi_z",
  12L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + habitat2020 + dox_z",
  13L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + habitat2020 + secchi_z + dox_z",
  14L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + habitat2020",
  15L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + dox_z",
  16L,  "out30_z * (distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z) + secchi_z + dox_z",
  17L,  "out30_z + secchi_z",
  18L,  "out30_z + distance_m_z + secchi_z",
  19L,  "out30_z + distance_along_channel_z + secchi_z",
  20L,  "out30_z * distance_m_z + secchi_z",
  21L,  "out30_z * distance_along_channel_z + secchi_z"
)
# Salinity / temperature fits 22-26 and the water-year diagnostic fit 27 are defined and run
# in appendix_salinity_temperature_wateryear/A04_edsm_salinity_temperature_wateryear_fits.R.

# Build the full brms formula for a given fixed-effects string.
build_station_formula <- function(fixef) {
  rhs <- c(fixef, "s(water_year_day)", "offset(log(Volume))", "(1|StationCode)")
  rhs <- rhs[nzchar(trimws(rhs))]          # drop empty fixef (null model)
  as.formula(paste("n_l_75 ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
}

# Fit ONE model with the (1|StationCode) intercept, run station K-fold on the cached folds,
# save the fit, append its summary to the printout file, then free memory.
fit_station_model <- function(num, fixef, folds,
                              data    = tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona,
                              priors  = catch_priors,
                              iter    = 3000,
                              warmup  = 2000,
                              chains  = 4,
                              control = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99)) {
  form <- build_station_formula(fixef)
  message("=== Fitting fit_edsm_", num, " ===")
  print(form)

  fit <- brm(
    formula = form,
    family  = negbinomial(link = "log"),
    data    = data,
    prior   = priors,
    iter    = iter, warmup = warmup, chains = chains,
    control = control,
    # all = FALSE: k-fold (unlike the old moment-matching) doesn't need the auxiliary
    # draws, so we drop the z_1/zs_* blocks. group = TRUE (default) keeps the per-station
    # r_StationCode draws that DHARMa and station-level plots rely on.
    save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE)
  )

  fit <- add_station_kfold(
    fit = fit, folds = folds,
    chains = chains, iter = iter, warmup = warmup, control = control
  )

  saveRDS(fit, file = sprintf("fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_%d.rds", num))

  # Keep the printout exactly as before -> same designated txt file.
  fileConn <- file("fits_edsm_Vfix/edsm_fits_Vfix_output.txt", open = "a")
  cat(sprintf("\n\n\nSummary of fit_edsm_%d:\n\n", num), file = fileConn)
  cat(capture.output(summary(fit)), file = fileConn, sep = "\n")
  close(fileConn)

  rm(fit); gc()
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Loop over a set of fit numbers (e.g. the ones not yet rerun with the intercept).
run_station_fits <- function(nums, defs = fit_defs, folds = station_folds, ...) {
  unknown <- setdiff(nums, defs$num)
  if (length(unknown)) {
    stop("No fixed-effects definition for fit number(s): ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
  }
  for (num in nums) {
    fixef <- defs$fixef[match(num, defs$num)]
    fit_station_model(num = num, fixef = fixef, folds = folds, ...)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# --- core-aware k-fold parallelism -------------------------------------------------
# Folds are parallelized across `workers`; each fold still runs `chains` chains. We never
# oversubscribe: workers = floor(cores / chains). With chains = 4 that gives 2 fold-workers
# on the 8-core machine and 1 (= sequential) on the 4-core machine -- no edits needed per box.
kfold_workers <- function(chains = 4) {
  nc <- parallel::detectCores()
  if (is.na(nc)) nc <- 1L
  max(1L, nc %/% chains)
}

# Set the future plan that brms::kfold uses to dispatch folds. Call this once before running.
# Pass workers = 1 to force sequential (e.g. if nested parallelism misbehaves on macOS).
setup_kfold_plan <- function(chains = 4, workers = NULL) {
  library(future)
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 3 * 1024^3)
  if (is.null(workers)) workers <- kfold_workers(chains)
  if (workers >= 2L) plan(multisession, workers = workers) else plan(sequential)
  message(sprintf("Cores: %s | chains/fold: %d | fold-workers: %d (%s)",
                  parallel::detectCores(), chains, workers,
                  if (workers >= 2L) "folds run in parallel" else "folds run sequentially"))
  invisible(workers)
}
```


###################################
Runtime check (optional).
Times a short pilot fit on the real model + data, then extrapolates to one full fit + K-fold and
to a batch of models. Auto-detects cores so the estimate matches how `setup_kfold_plan()` will run
(8 cores -> 2 folds at a time; 4 cores -> sequential). Does NOT run a full fit.
########################################
```{r runtime-check, eval=FALSE}
estimate_fit_time <- function(fixef       = "out30_z + secchi_z",
                              nW          = 250L, nDraw = 200L,   # pilot iters
                              prod_warmup = 2000, prod_sample = 1000,
                              K = 5, chains = 4, n_models = 15,
                              workers = NULL,
                              data = tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona, priors = catch_priors) {
  if (is.null(workers)) workers <- kfold_workers(chains)

  # Short pilot on the real model structure -- the costly bits (1005-level RE + smooth) are shared
  # by every model, so a simple fixed-effects set is representative for timing.
  pilot <- brm(
    build_station_formula(fixef),
    family = negbinomial("log"), data = data, prior = priors,
    chains = 1, warmup = nW, iter = nW + nDraw,
    control = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
    refresh = 0, seed = 1
  )

  et     <- rstan::get_elapsed_time(pilot$fit)          # per-chain warmup / sample seconds
  Tchain <- (et[1, "warmup"] / nW)   * prod_warmup +    # extrapolate to production iters
            (et[1, "sample"] / nDraw) * prod_sample
  waves      <- ceiling(K / workers)                    # k-fold runs in this many sequential waves
  kfold_wall <- waves * ((K - 1) / K) * Tchain          # each fold trains on ~ (K-1)/K of the rows
  per_model  <- Tchain + kfold_wall                     # main fit (chains in parallel) + k-fold

  cat(sprintf("cores=%s  chains=%d  fold-workers=%d  ->  %d k-fold wave(s)\n",
              parallel::detectCores(), chains, workers, waves))
  cat(sprintf("single full fit : %4.1f min\n", Tchain / 60))
  cat(sprintf("one model       : %4.1f min  (%.2f h)\n", per_model / 60, per_model / 3600))
  cat(sprintf("%2d models        : %4.1f h\n", n_models, n_models * per_model / 3600))
  invisible(per_model)
}

estimate_fit_time()                          # k = 5 on whichever machine you're on
# estimate_fit_time(K = 10, n_models = 3)    # what k = 10 on the top few models would cost
```


###################################
Run the models.
Each fit + K-fold is slow (~1-2 h per model); run this interactively, not on knit.
NOTE: fit_station_model() writes fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_<N>.rds unconditionally, so only run
the numbers you actually intend to (re)fit.
########################################
```{r run-fits, eval=FALSE}
# Auto-detect cores and parallelize k-fold folds accordingly: 8 cores -> 2 folds at a time,
# 4 cores -> sequential. chains stays 4 either way. Use setup_kfold_plan(workers = 1) to force
# sequential if nested parallelism misbehaves on macOS.
setup_kfold_plan(chains = 4)

# Make sure the cached folds are loaded (the canonical-fold-set chunk above creates them).
station_folds <- readRDS("fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_folds.rds")

# The reported set is fits 0-21:
run_station_fits(0:21)
```


###################################
Harvest K-fold criteria into one small bundle (run ONCE; re-run only after adding/refitting models).
Loads each big fit one at a time, extracts ONLY its stored K-fold criterion, drops the fit from
memory (rm + gc), and saves the collected criteria as a single small RDS (a few MB). After this you
never reload the multi-GB fits for a comparison again — and it's immune to iCloud eviction because
the bundle stays small. tryCatch skips any unreadable/evicted fit with a warning instead of aborting.
########################################
```{r harvest-bundle, eval=FALSE}
fit_nums       <- 0:21                 # any subset that has been run is fine
criterion_name <- "kfold5_StationCode"
bundle_path    <- "fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_criteria_bundle.rds"

kfold_bundle <- list()
for (n in fit_nums) {
  fpath <- sprintf("fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_%d.rds", n)
  if (!file.exists(fpath)) next
  nm <- paste0("fit_edsm_", n)
  crit <- tryCatch({
    fit <- readRDS(fpath)                          # one big fit in memory...
    out <- fit$criteria[[criterion_name]]          # ...keep only the K-fold criterion
    rm(fit); gc()                                  # ...drop it before the next one
    if (is.null(out)) warning(nm, " has no '", criterion_name, "' criterion")
    out
  }, error = function(e) { warning(nm, ": ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  if (!is.null(crit)) kfold_bundle[[nm]] <- crit
}

if (!dir.exists("fits_edsm_Vfix")) dir.create("fits_edsm_Vfix")
saveRDS(kfold_bundle, bundle_path)
cat("bundled", length(kfold_bundle), "of", length(fit_nums), "fits ->", bundle_path, "\n")
```


###################################
K-fold model comparison from the bundle (fast, re-runnable, never touches the big fits).
########################################
```{r compare-kfold, eval=FALSE}
bundle_path  <- "fits_edsm_Vfix/kfold5_station_criteria_bundle.rds"
kfold_bundle <- Filter(Negate(is.null), readRDS(bundle_path))

if (length(kfold_bundle) < 2) {
  stop("Need at least two fits in the bundle to compare; re-run the harvest chunk.")
}

# ELPD comparison ranking (best model on top, elpd_diff relative to it)
kfold_comparisons_catch_u75 <- loo_compare(kfold_bundle)
print(kfold_comparisons_catch_u75)

write.csv(
  as.data.frame(kfold_comparisons_catch_u75),
  "fits_edsm_Vfix/fit_edsm_topmods_catch_kfold5_station_comparisons.csv"
)
```
